route: /style-board/ (the style board: module process:band, longest and shortest copy, photos as grey frames)

findings.issue: The band still has no heading: a body-size lead ("Our full-package service, from brief to shipment.") sits directly above the steps, so the section has no title at either width.
findings.reference: The competitor's band opens with an eyebrow ("HOW IT WORKS") and a large H2 ("Six steps from Costing to delivery") above the rule that leads into the steps.
findings.fix: Site Factory should give this process block a heading (e.g. "Seven steps from brief to shipment") so h2.process__heading renders above the lead.

findings.issue: The band still has neither a heading nor a lead. Five bare steps start under an empty band of top padding (also on phones, about 100 px before the first rule), so the dark section has no visible purpose.
findings.reference: The competitor's band always opens with an eyebrow and an H2 naming the process before the numbered steps.
findings.fix: Site Factory should give faq-steps a heading (e.g. "How a consulting project runs") and, if it has one, a short lead.

findings.issue: The step numbers are still white like the body text, and the band's rule still runs level with the first row's numbers (patterns.css .process-steps::before, top: 22px) rather than above them. The second row (05–07) has no rule at all, so the numbers do not read as an accent and the two rows are styled differently.
findings.reference: The competitor sets its step numbers ("01"–"06") small, bold and in its light-blue accent, a clear space below one full-width rule that sits under the heading and above every step.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set --process-marker-text on .block--process[data-variant="band"] to the light accent (the button's cyan). For min-width 768px, move the band's .process-steps::before to top: 0 with left/right: 0, and give .process-steps padding-top (about 2rem) so the one rule stands above both rows of numbers.
